title: Revit Materials and Appearance Implementation
purpose: Apply governed Revit material naming, classification, graphic appearance, and render appearance while keeping example material codes and unresolved numeric values noncanonical.
preconditions: Applicable material naming/classification rules are available from governed standards or registries.
Approved appearance assets or controlled material libraries are available where required.

steps.name: Use governed material identity
actions: Name and classify materials using the applicable governed S4/S8 syntax and classification context.
Do not create project-local material aliases that duplicate an existing governed material without an approved reason.
validation: Material names are consistent and unambiguous.
Duplicate or conflicting material identities are identified for remediation.

steps.name: Coordinate documentation and render appearance
actions: Use material graphics for governed cut/surface patterns and colors where applicable.
Use controlled appearance assets for rendered/PBR appearance.
Keep documentation graphics and render appearance coordinated but recognize that they are separate Revit material surfaces.
validation: Graphic and appearance assets are assigned consistently for the material's intended use.
No uncontrolled appearance asset path or duplicate asset is introduced where a governed library exists.

steps.name: Resolve graphics through governed hierarchy
actions: Coordinate material-driven hatches and graphics with governed Object Styles, Category/Subcategory Graphics, and View Templates.
Avoid per-element overrides as a substitute for material/category/filter governance.
validation: Material-based display does not conflict with the governed graphics hierarchy.
Recurring display exceptions are handled through governed templates/filters/material definitions.

outputs: Revit materials with governed identity and coordinated documentation/render appearance
future_dependencies: Approved PBR asset locations and lifecycle rules
governance_notes: Source material naming tables are marked example-only and are not promoted.
Unconfirmed numeric appearance or pattern values remain unresolved until separately governed.

provenance.migration_note: Migrated durable material-governance practices only; example names and unconfirmed values remain noncanonical.
